top_signals.title: Oil Slides Nearly 4% as Returning Supply Outweighs Gulf Attacks
top_signals.summary: Crude prices deepened their slide on Monday even as Wall Street rallied on Nvidia's reinstatement of chief executive Jensen Huang, with West Texas Intermediate (WTI) trading at its weakest level since late August. At 10:29 a.m. ET, WTI was down 3.5% at $80.50 per barrel, Brent was down 3.6% at 89.23 dollars, and U.S. natural gas futures had fallen 8.2% to 3.130 dollars per million British thermal units. Nvidia said it was reinstating Jensen Huang as president, chief executive and board director, effective immediately, 11 days after he resigned.…

top_signals.title: Libya’s Oil Output Plunges as Armed Groups Shut Key Pipelines
top_signals.summary: Libya’s oil production has crashed by about 350,000 barrels per day (bpd) after an outlaw group closed a valve on the pipeline transporting crude oil from Sharara, the country’s biggest oilfield, the National Oil Corporation said on Monday. Libya’s NOC condemned the closure, which adds to the closure of a pipeline at the Hamada oilfield, which has been ongoing for three weeks now and has already resulted in a loss of about 15,000 bpd of crude oil production.  This weekend, NOC said that the forced shutdown of the Hamada pipeline…
